text.en: Meena saw a potato sprout and a seed sprout. "Plants multiply in more than one way," said her teacher.

Vegetative reproduction produces a new plant from a part like a stem, root or leaf, and asexual reproduction forms new individuals without gametes, as by spores or budding. Sexual reproduction in flowering plants happens in the flower, with male stamens and female carpels, and the ovule contains the egg.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma, either self or cross, with agents such as wind, water, insects and birds. After compatible pollination, a pollen tube can carry male gametes to an ovule. One fuses with the egg to form a zygote. After fertilisation, the ovule typically becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.
In humans, the male reproductive organs include the testes and the female includes the ovary. Gametogenesis is the making of sperms and ova, the menstrual cycle involves recurring changes in the ovaries and uterus, with variable timing. Following fertilisation and implantation, development progresses through embryo and foetal stages.
Vegetative reproduction produces a new plant from a part like a stem, root or leaf, and asexual reproduction forms new individuals without gametes, as by spores or budding.
Sexual reproduction in flowering plants happens in the flower, with male stamens and female carpels, and the ovule contains the egg.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma, either self or cross, with agents such as wind, water, insects and birds.

After compatible pollen reaches the stigma, a pollen tube can grow towards an ovule. A male gamete can fuse with the egg to form a zygote. Typically the ovule develops into a seed and the ovary develops into a fruit.
In humans, the male reproductive organs include the testes and the female includes the ovary.

Gametogenesis is the formation of gametes. The menstrual cycle involves recurring changes in the ovaries and uterus, and its timing varies. After fertilisation and implantation, development progresses through embryo and foetal stages.
Reproduction helps continue a species through new generations. Both plants and animals have different ways of producing offspring.
A single parent can produce new individuals without fusion of gametes. Offspring are usually genetically very similar to the parent.

board.text: Asexual reproduction does not fuse gametes

text.en: A potato is a stem tuber. The small eyes are buds, and a new shoot can grow from one of those buds.

board.text: A stem tuber can produce a shoot

text.en: A new plant can grow from a suitable root or leaf in some species. In Bryophyllum, small plantlets can form along the leaf margins.

board.text: Vegetative reproduction can use other organs

text.en: In textbook examples such as Hydra, a small bud grows out from the parent and can become a separate individual.
In some organisms, spores can survive dispersal and grow when conditions permit. These spores are different from seeds.

board.text: Spores may grow into a new stage

text.en: A gamete is a reproductive cell. Sexual reproduction involves fusion of gametes, combining genetic information.
The anther is the pollen-producing part of the stamen. A filament often supports the anther.
The stigma receives pollen. The style connects it to the ovary, and the ovary contains one or more ovules.

board.text: A carpel has a stigma, style and ovary

text.en: Pollen can reach the stigma of the same flower, another flower on the same plant or a flower on another plant of the same species.

board.text: Pollination moves pollen to the stigma

text.en: Cross-pollination transfers pollen between different plants of the same species. The agent may be wind, an insect or another animal.
An insect may carry pollen between flowers while visiting them. Wind-pollinated plants often release large quantities of light pollen.

board.text: Flower features can help transfer pollen

text.en: Pollination puts pollen at the stigma. In fertilisation, a gamete from the pollen fuses with the egg inside an ovule.

board.text: Pollination and fertilisation are separate events

text.en: A compatible pollen grain can germinate on the stigma. A pollen tube grows towards an ovule and carries the male gametes.

board.text: A pollen tube grows through the style

text.en: One male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote. Another fuses with the central cell to begin forming nutritive tissue called endosperm.
The zygote develops into the embryo within the seed. The ovary typically becomes a fruit around the seed or seeds.

board.text: An ovule typically becomes a seed

text.en: A mature seed can begin to germinate under suitable conditions. Water, oxygen and an appropriate temperature are generally important.
In humans, testes produce sperm cells and ovaries produce egg cells. They also release hormones involved in growth and reproduction.
The ovaries and uterus undergo changes during the menstrual cycle. Ovulation means an egg cell is released from an ovary.
The uterine lining builds up during part of the cycle. If a pregnancy does not begin, part of the lining is shed during menstruation.
When sperm and egg fuse, they form a zygote. The early embryo divides while it moves towards the uterus.

board.text: Fertilisation usually occurs in an oviduct

text.en: The developing embryo attaches to the lining of the uterus. Later, the placenta allows exchange of oxygen, nutrients and wastes between the two circulations.

board.text: Implantation is attachment to the uterine lining

text.en: An embryo develops body structures early in pregnancy. In the foetal stage, those structures continue growing and maturing.
Pollination is specific to plants. Gamete fusion forms a zygote in both plants and animals that reproduce sexually. The later structures differ.

board.text: Compare the stages without mixing the terms

text.en: Pollen is made in the anther.
It must reach the stigma.
This transfer is pollination.

problem.en: A potato grows a new shoot from one of its eyes. Which kind of reproduction does this illustrate?

text.en: Identify the eye as a bud on a stem tuber.

why.en: The new shoot grows from an existing plant organ.

text.en: It is vegetative reproduction.

why.en: No fusion of gametes takes place to make that shoot.

problem.en: An insect moves pollen from the anther of a flower to the stigma of another plant of the same species. Has fertilisation already occurred?

text.en: The motion transfers pollen between plants.
Fertilisation still requires gamete fusion inside an ovule.

why.en: A pollen tube may grow after compatible pollen lands on the stigma.

problem.en: What do the ovule and ovary typically become after fertilisation?

text.en: The ovule develops into a seed.
The ovary develops into a fruit.

why.en: The fruit typically encloses one or more seeds.

prompt.en: A friend says Fertilisation happens before pollination. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Then the pollen tube leads to fertilisation.

points.en: Pollination moves pollen to the stigma.
